exercises.instruction: Read the passage and answer the questions.
exercises.passage:
Starting Over at Thirty-Five

Changing careers in your thirties can feel like throwing away a decade of effort. In practice, little is wasted: a teacher who becomes a trainer, or a nurse who moves into health technology, carries across communication skills, patience, and professional contacts. Experience transfers more often than people expect.

The practical barriers are real, however. Retraining usually means evening courses after full working days, and an entry-level salary in a new field may be lower than the old one. Successful changers plan for this gap by saving several months of expenses before resigning and by testing the new field first, through freelance projects, volunteering, or shadowing a professional for a week.

The deepest obstacle is often psychological. Admitting that a chosen path no longer fits can feel like failure, when it is really information. People who treat the move as a reversible, time-limited experiment adapt faster than those who demand a guarantee before the first step.
